1.note: The term **saying** introduces a direct quotation. See how you translated **saying** in [1:1](ta:01).

2.q: צַ֚ו אֶת בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵ⁠הֶ֑ם
2.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Command the sons of Israel to keep presenting to me at its appointed time my offering, my bread for my gifts, a scent of my pleasing]

Yahweh is using one kind of food, **my bread**, to mean food in general. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my food]

Here, a **gift** is a kind of offering presented to Yahweh by burning it on the altar. If your readers would not be familiar with what a gift is in this sense, you could use the name of a similar practice that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [for my offerings made by fire]

Yahweh is using **you shall keep to present to me** as a common expression of the culture to mean “you shall be careful to present to me.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you must be sure to present to me]

3.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And you shall tell them that this is the gift that they shall present to Yahweh: perfect male lambs, sons of a year, two for the day, a continual burnt offering]

Offering animals that were **perfect**, that is, animals that had no defect, was a symbolic action by which the Israelites showed that they were giving Yahweh what was most valuable and complete. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [male lambs without any defect, showing that you give Yahweh the best]

Yahweh is using **sons of a year** as a common expression of the culture to mean “one year old.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [that are a year old]

4.note: Yahweh is using **you shall do** as a common expression of the culture to mean “you shall offer as a sacrifice.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The one male lamb you shall offer as a sacrifice in the morning]
The word **you** is singular here. It may refer to the individual person who offered the lamb. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

Yahweh is using **between the evenings** as a common expression of the culture to mean “at twilight.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [at twilight]

5.note: A **tenth** means one part out of ten equal parts.

This **ephah** was equivalent to 22 liters or nearly two thirds of a bushel. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express this in terms of modern measurements, either in the text or in a footnote.

The expression **mixed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [which you have mixed with beaten oil]

Here, **beaten oil** is a kind of olive oil that people made by pounding olives rather than by pressing them. If your readers would not be familiar with what beaten oil is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [with high-quality olive oil]
A **fourth** means one part out of four equal parts.

This **hin** was equivalent to about 3.7 liters or about one gallon. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express this in terms of modern measurements, either in the text or in a footnote.

6.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **continuity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a continual burnt offering]

This could mean: (1) that the Israelites had already offered this kind of sacrifice at **Mount Sinai**. Alternate translation: [the one you already performed at Mount Sinai] (2) that God had already instituted this kind of sacrifice at **Mount Sinai**. Alternate translation: [the one I instituted at Mount Sinai]

The expression **done** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the one that your ancestors offered at Mount Sinai]

7.note: The pronoun **its** refers to the continual burnt offering that Yahweh has just described. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the drink offering for that burnt offering]

This could mean: (1) the outer room of the tabernacle, the Holy Place. Alternate translation: [In the outer room of the tabernacle] (2) any holy place, including courtyard around the tabernacle. Alternate translation: [In a holy area]

The implication is that the priest is the one who pours out this drink offering. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [In the holy place the priest shall pour out]

8.note: The word **you** is singular here. It may refer to the individual person who offered the lamb. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.
See how you translated these same phrases in Numbers 28:4. Alternate translation: [at twilight]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Like the grain offering of the morning and like its drink offering, so you shall offer a grain offering and a drink offering with this male lamb]

9.note: Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [And on the day of the Sabbath you shall offer two male lambs]

10.note: Yahweh is using **a burnt offering of a Sabbath on its Sabbath** as a common expression of the culture to mean “a burnt offering for every Sabbath.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [A burnt offering to be presented on every Sabbath]

The implication is that the Israelites are to present this offering in addition to the continual burnt offering, not in place of it. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [in addition to the regular burnt offering]

11.note: Yahweh is using **at the heads of your months** as a common expression of the culture to mean “on the first day of each month.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And on the first day of every month]

This could mean: (1) that all the animals were **perfect**. Alternate translation: [and all the animals must be perfect] (2) that the **lambs** were **perfect**. Alternate translation: [each lamb perfect]

Yahweh is using **sons of cattle** as a common expression of the culture to mean “young bulls.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [which are young]

13.note: Yahweh is repeating the phrase **a tenth** in order to express the idea that this amount applies to each male lamb individually. If your language can repeat words in this way, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing this idea. Alternate translation: [and one tenth of an ephah each of]

14.q: וְ⁠נִסְכֵּי⁠הֶ֗ם חֲצִ֣י הַ⁠הִין֩ יִהְיֶ֨ה לַ⁠פָּ֜ר וּ⁠שְׁלִישִׁ֧ת הַ⁠הִ֣ין לָ⁠אַ֗יִל וּ⁠רְבִיעִ֥ת הַ⁠הִ֛ין לַ⁠כֶּ֖בֶשׂ יָ֑יִן
14.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **wine** with the information about how much is to be presented for each animal. Alternate translation: [And their drink offerings of wine shall be the half of the hin for the bull, and the third of the hin for the ram, and the fourth of the hin for the male lamb]

14.q: חֲצִ֣י הַ⁠הִין֩ יִהְיֶ֨ה לַ⁠פָּ֜ר וּ⁠שְׁלִישִׁ֧ת הַ⁠הִ֣ין לָ⁠אַ֗יִל
14.note: A **half** means one part out of two equal parts. A **third** means one part out of three equal parts.

15.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **buck** that is characterized by being one of the animals called **goats**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and one male goat]

The expression **it shall be done** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the priests shall offer it in addition to the burnt offering of the continuity]

16.note: The **first** month of the Hebrew calendar includes the last part of March and the first part of April on Western calendars. You could convert the Hebrew day and month into an approximate date on the calendar that your culture uses. However, the Jews used a lunar calendar, so if you use a solar calendar, the date will be different every year, and the translation will not be entirely accurate. So you may just want to give the number of the day and the name of the month on the Hebrew calendar and say in a footnote approximately what time of year that is on your calendar.

If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **day 14**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use, such as “the fourteenth day.” Alternate translation: [on the fourteenth day of the month]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **Passover** that is characterized by being celebrated in honor of Yahweh. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the Passover celebrated in honor of Yahweh]

17.note: This could mean: (1) that the **festival** itself lasted for seven days. Alternate translation: [is a festival for seven days, during which unleavened bread] (2) that the **festival** lasted one day, but for that day and the following six days the Israelites had to eat **unleavened bread**. Alternate translation: [is a one day festival. For seven days, starting with that day, unleavened bread]

The expression **shall be eaten** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread]

Yahweh is using **seven days** as a common expression of the culture to mean “during each of the seven days.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Throughout the seven days]

18.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **holiness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [a holy assembly]

The phrase **work of service** expresses a single idea. The word **service** tells more about **work**. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [any ordinary labor]

19.note: The implication is that the Israelites must choose animals that have no defects, since Yahweh accepts only animals of that kind. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [They shall be without any defect, as Yahweh requires]

20.q: וּ⁠מִ֨נְחָתָ֔⁠ם סֹ֖לֶת בְּלוּלָ֣ה בַ⁠שָּׁ֑מֶן שְׁלֹשָׁ֨ה עֶשְׂרֹנִ֜ים לַ⁠פָּ֗ר וּ⁠שְׁנֵ֧י עֶשְׂרֹנִ֛ים לָ⁠אַ֖יִל תַּעֲשֽׂוּ
20.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about what the Israelites are to **do** with the information about **their grain offering**. Alternate translation: [And you shall offer as their grain offering flour mixed with the oil, three tenths for the bull and two tenths for the ram]

21.note: The word **you** is singular here. It may refer to the individual person who offered the lamb. So use the singular form in your translation if your language marks that distinction.

The implication is that the Israelites are to present this amount of flour for each one of the seven male lambs. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [for each one of the seven male lambs]

22.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **atonement**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [to take away your sin]

23.note: The word **Besides** introduces something additional. If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [In addition to the burnt offering of the morning]
The pronoun **these** refers to the offerings that Yahweh has just described. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [you shall offer these sacrifices]

24.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **bread** that is characterized by being a **gift** that the Israelites present to him. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [bread that is a gift]

25.note: See how you translated this same phrase in Numbers 28:18. Alternate translation: [a holy assembly]
See how you translated this same phrase in Numbers 28:18. Alternate translation: [any ordinary work]

26.note: Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **day** that is characterized by the presenting of the **firstfruits**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And on the day set apart for the firstfruits]

The word that the ULT translates as **when** indicates that the Israelites are to hold an assembly of holiness at the same time as when they present a new grain offering to Yahweh. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could describe the time relationship more explicitly. Alternate translation: [at the same time that you present a new grain offering to Yahweh in your weeks]

The implication is that the phrase **in your weeks** refers to the Festival of Weeks, which the Israelites celebrated seven weeks after they began to harvest their grain. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [during your Festival of Weeks]
See how you translated this same phrase in Numbers 28:25. Alternate translation: [a holy assembly]
See how you translated this same phrase in Numbers 28:25. Alternate translation: [any ordinary work]

30.note: See how you translated these same phrases in Numbers 28:22. Alternate translation: [to take away your sin]

31.q: מִ⁠לְּ⁠בַ֞ד עֹלַ֧ת הַ⁠תָּמִ֛יד וּ⁠מִנְחָת֖⁠וֹ תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ תְּמִימִ֥ם יִהְיוּ לָ⁠כֶ֖ם וְ⁠נִסְכֵּי⁠הֶֽם
31.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **their drink offerings** with the information about what the Israelites are to **do**. Alternate translation: [Besides the burnt offering of the continuity and its grain offering you shall do, and their drink offerings; they shall be perfect for you]

The word **Besides** introduces something additional. If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [In addition to the burnt offering of the continuity and its grain offering]

Here, the pronoun **their** could refer to: (1) the burnt offerings for the day of firstfruits and the **burnt offering of the continuity**. Alternate translation: [and the drink offerings for all the offerings] (2) just the burnt offerings for the day of firstfruits. Alternate translation: [and the drink offerings for the offerings of the day of firstfruits] (3) just the **burnt offering of the continuity**. Alternate translation: [and the drink offering for the burnt offering of the continuity]
